facts: The whole site, yards included, is already one module grid by design: CL9SiteLayout.h:14 says the site is entirely a module grid, the yard as much as the barn interior. Outdoor modules exist as rows: yard_gate (Start, 3x2) and yard_open (Normal, 3x3, bOutdoor), per docs/plan/data/module.md:76 and :84.

Site-local frame: (0,0) is the truck pad and +X points into the grid (CL9SiteLayout.h:19). Layout.Origin = (EntryOffset, -Span*CellSize/2) (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:871). The Start module is pinned to grid column 0 at mid-Y (cpp:889), and its entry door always faces -X/West (cpp:906-908). The generator has no whole-layout rotation.

The grid is always square, Span x Span (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:866-870), with Span = clamp(ceil(sqrt(N*6))*2, 16, 128). For farm, N=200 gives 70 and day 10 (x1.25 = 250) gives 78, so a higher cap does not move henhouse, farm or pigfarm hashes. N=1000 needs 156 and N=1250 needs 174. Memory at 256^2 x 2 floors is under 1 MB.

setup_stage.py:79 duplicates the Span formula by hand, including the 128 cap. setup_stage.py:77-82 and :150-196 size the floor actors and the NavMeshBoundsVolume from one square grid in +X from the pad. LARGEST_DAY_SCALE = 1.25 is set at setup_stage.py:41.

Single-layout container: ACL9SiteMap holds one FCL9SiteLayout plus one FCL9SiteParams (CL9SiteMap.h:114-115). It is documented as one per world (h:16-17). Find returns the first actor (CL9SiteMap.cpp:171-175), Rebuild anchors to the first ACL9TruckPad (cpp:191-195), and SiteToWorld is translation-only with a zero-rotation actor (cpp:210, 238-242).

One RNG stream per layout: FRandomStream Rng(Seed) (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:873). The lamp RNG is seeded from Layout.Seed^0x5A17 (CL9SiteMap.cpp:653). Prop and variant picks hash site-local coordinates, not an RNG (CL9SiteMap.cpp:40-56, 703). Only one seed is replicated (CL9GameState.cpp:382-385, 401). Seed 0 means nothing is built (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:842), so any derived sub-seed must avoid 0.

GrowFloor computes the lead-phase main path from the whole-site Params.ModuleCount, not from the Budget it is given: MainCount = min(Remaining, max(2, round(Params.ModuleCount*MainPathShare))) (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:540). Calling it per district without a fix would give every district a 300-module spine at N=1000.

SpecialCopies placement takes random frontier spots right after the main path, across the whole floor's frontier (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:554-572). Nothing guarantees one delivery room per region of a big layout.

Depth is hop-based and global to one layout. PointsOfPurpose sorts by Hops (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1198). PointsInDepthBand normalises by that layout's MaxHops (cpp:1206-1214). GameMode evaluates Site.Zones once against one layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:600-613). decisions.md:1602-1603 rejected cm-distance bands in favour of hop depth.

GameMode::SpawnNight is the only runtime consumer of the layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-646). It takes one GetLayout(). The site-wide monsters list uses the deepest 60% of the hop-sorted list (cpp:525, 595). Jar dedupe is keyed on FCL9LevelPoint::Module, a per-layout module index (cpp:625-633). Monsters do not read the layout at all (CL9Monster.cpp has no SiteMap or LevelPoint use).

Exactly one emergency exit per layout: CarveEmergencyExit sets one Flap on floor 0 (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:430-471). Tests assert exactly one (CL9SiteLayoutTests.cpp:178, 263, 596, 610). module.md:190-197 (decision 3) fixes it as a constant: one entrance (yard_gate), one flapIn.

IsConnected does a BFS from module 0 (the Start) and follows only Door edges (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1220-1261). LayoutHash covers one layout's modules and edge bytes (cpp:1264-1281) and is logged once (CL9SiteMap.cpp:630-634).

An edge between two outdoor modules is still a fence wall, or a fence with a DoorWidth gap. WallKind returns 'wall' (fence) when both sides are outdoor (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1072-1083), and AddEdge always emits stubs plus a door gap for a Door (cpp:1101-1113). A yard made of yard_open modules is therefore a chain of fenced 15 m paddocks joined by about 2.5 m gates, not an open road.

SealEdges turns every edge between two different modules into a Wall (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:395-400). Adjacent modules get a Door only along the growth parent link, or by LoopChance in OpenNeighbours (cpp:299-308).

Module rows have no fallback across themes: a stage's module set is one whole set (CL9SiteDef.h:199-207). farm inherits theme 'henhouse' (farm.json inherit_from; setup_stage.py:35 INHERIT includes 'theme'). Adding an outdoor road row to the henhouse theme would change the Pools and RNG draws for henhouse, farm and pigfarm.

ISM components are keyed only by (kind, mesh) for the whole site (CL9SiteMap.cpp:402-405) and by (mesh, solid) for props (cpp:658-661), all attached to one actor. Nothing in the data or the components supports per-district culling today.

PlaceProps runs a warning check that loops over every Layout.Points entry for every solid prop (CL9SiteMap.cpp:769-783) and every door gap (cpp:759-768). That is O(props x points), quadratic in site size, and every client runs it on every build. BuildPoints emits points contiguously in module order (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:477-498), so a per-module index range is available.

Ground outside the modules is walkable level floor: setup_stage scales the Floor/Ground actors to the grid rect plus MARGIN 2500 (setup_stage.py:44, 172-196), and the flap opens onto that ground. Bare ground between districts would carry no fences, lamps, props or level points, and no hop continuity.

Current proof at size: CL9.Map.LargeSite runs N=200 over 30 seeds and logs ms per layout (CL9SiteLayoutTests.cpp:541-617). CL9.Map.DepthBand runs N=200 on seed 873 (cpp:619-658). Neither has run at N >= 1000.

objections.target: Draft: K independent CL9SiteLayout instances, each with its own sub-seed and world origin
objections.problem: Every runtime consumer assumes one layout, so K layouts push changes into the consumers. ACL9SiteMap holds one Layout and one Params, and Find() returns the first actor, so K actors would break Find. GameMode::SpawnNight reads one GetLayout(), and its jar dedupe is keyed on a per-layout module index, so concatenated points would collide and drop jars. PointsOfPurpose and the 60% deepest slice sort by per-layout hops, so concatenating points would interleave districts meaningfully wrong. LayoutHash and IsConnected only describe one layout, so nothing proves the whole stage is connected. The generator does stay untouched, but in exchange the SiteMap container, PointToWorld, SpawnNight, the zone semantics, the hash/log and new composition tests all have to change.
objections.alternative: Keep ONE FCL9SiteLayout and grow districts inside it (multi-root growth, see recommendations). SiteMap, GameMode, jars, depth zones, IsConnected and the hash then stay as they are.

objections.target: Draft claim: keeping the 128-cell cap untouched is a benefit of K layouts
objections.problem: The cap is a single clamp constant, not a proven limit. Raising it cannot change henhouse, farm or pigfarm, because their day-10 Span is at most 78. The real cost of a bigger cap is updating the hand-copied formula in setup_stage.py:79. Protecting the cap buys nothing.
objections.evidence: CL9SiteLayout.cpp:866; setup_stage.py:79; farm.json base_module_count 200 x LARGEST_DAY_SCALE 1.25 gives 250, and 2*ceil(sqrt(1500)) = 78
objections.alternative: Raise the cap to 256, or derive it from the budget, gated so that Span < 128 sites are byte-identical. Expose the Span or extent computation to Python (a BlueprintCallable static) so setup_stage stops duplicating it.

objections.target: Draft: districts arranged around/along a yard, each with its own yard_gate facing the yard
objections.problem: A layout's gate always faces -X at column 0 and mid-Y, and the site has no rotation: SiteToWorld is translation only, FlapIn Outward is in site-local axes, and prop yaw is Module.Rotation*90. 'Around a yard' therefore needs a whole-layout 90/180-degree rotation pass over Modules, Sockets, EdgeX/EdgeY and Outward. Without it, every district must sit east of a single N-S yard strip, in one column. Each farm frame is 70 cells (350 m), so five of them make an elongated 1.75 km map unless footprints are measured after generation and packed. NavBounds and floor sizing in setup_stage are fixed at edit time, so they would have to cover the worst case of K frames.
objections.alternative: In a single grid, district placement is a property of where growth roots sit along a yard trunk. Districts can lie on both sides of an E-W yard with no rotation code, and the truck stays at the west edge, so setup_stage keeps its +X frame.

objections.target: Draft: depth zones evaluated per district; farther districts more dangerous
objections.problem: Per-district evaluation normalises each district's hops to [0,1], so every district gets identical outer/middle/deep bands. That contradicts 'farther district = more dangerous/valuable'. Making it work needs a new data axis (a per-district danger tier or zone set) that does not exist. The current Zones column cannot express it.
objections.alternative: In one grid, hops run truck → yard trunk → district gate → in-district, so a district farther along the trunk is deeper with no new data. Existing Zones and PointsInDepthBand work unchanged. A District id per placement can be added later if the designer wants per-district zone filters.

objections.target: Draft: each district gets its own yard_gate (Start) and its own emergency exit
objections.problem: K Start modules and K flaps contradict module.md decision 3 (exactly one entrance and one flapIn, fixed as a constant), and they break four assertions in the existing tests. This is a user-decision change the draft does not flag. The yard_gate is also the module 'the truck docks against', with a campfire set, so K of them reads as K truck stops.
objections.alternative: One Start (the truck's yard_gate) in one grid. Districts are entered through ordinary Door edges from yard modules. If one flap per district is wanted, raise it with the user as an explicit decision change to module.md decision 3 and record it in docs/decisions.md.

objections.target: Draft: outdoor yard joining the districts
objections.problem: In the K-layout design no code generates the inter-district yard: it would be bare level ground with no fences, lamps, campfires, props, Monster/Loot points or hops. Inside the generator, a yard built from yard_open modules is a run of fenced paddocks joined by about 2.5 m gates, because outdoor-to-outdoor edges still emit 'wall' fence segments and stubs. Neither design yields a road or an open yard.
objections.alternative: Add a rule gated by a site column: between two bOutdoor modules, always set Door in OpenNeighbours (LoopChance = 1 for outdoor pairs), and have BuildSegments emit no segment for Door edges whose two sides are both outdoor. Keep the edge byte as Door so IsConnected (Door-only BFS, cpp:1248) still proves connectivity. The perimeter facing INDEX_NONE keeps its wall.

objections.target: Draft: SpecialCopies per district gives each district its jars
objections.problem: This holds for K layouts. In any single-grid variant it does not hold automatically, because Specials take random spots on the whole floor frontier right after the main path. GrowFloor also sizes the main path from Params.ModuleCount instead of its Budget. Both single-site assumptions have to be fixed whenever growth is split by region.
objections.alternative: Run the lead phases (spine, then Specials) once per district with a private frontier seeded at that district's root. Compute MainCount from the district budget, not Params.ModuleCount. With DistrictCount > 0, SpecialCopies means copies per district.

objections.target: Draft: new stage inherits the henhouse module set and only adds rows
objections.problem: Module rows are a whole set per Theme with no fallback, and farm and pigfarm inherit theme 'henhouse'. Adding any row to that theme, such as an outdoor road Passage, changes the Pools for henhouse, farm and pigfarm. That changes their layouts and breaks the out-of-scope rule 'no changes to henhouse/farm/pigfarm'.
objections.alternative: Either give the giant stage its own Theme (copy the 19 module rows plus new outdoor road rows; pieces fall back to the shared rows), or pick the trunk pool by bOutdoor so the existing yard_open is enough and no rows are added. Measure whether a yard_open-only trunk is acceptable before adding any rows.

objections.target: Draft: per-district culling by distance/visibility
objections.problem: ISM components are keyed per kind and mesh across the whole site, under one actor. K layouts do not give per-district components for free unless they become K actors, which breaks Find(). Separately, the PlaceProps diagnostic loops are quadratic, about 25 times the farm cost at 5x, and every client pays them on every build.
objections.alternative: Add a chunk id to both ComponentFor keys: the district id from the placement, or a spatial tile. That works the same with either design. Index points by module (they are contiguous per module) or skip the overlap warnings outside the editor.

recommendations: Recommended smallest change: multi-root growth in ONE grid, active only when the new column DistrictCount > 0. With DistrictCount == 0 the code path stays byte-identical, so henhouse, farm and pigfarm do not change. Steps: (1) place the Start as today; (2) lay a yard trunk with a deepest-first main path whose pool is filtered to bOutdoor && Type in {Normal, Passage}; (3) pick K roots on trunk frontier spots by trunk-hop quantiles, alternating N and S sides; (4) for each district, run GrowFloor's lead phases plus branch phase with a private frontier seeded only at its root and budget B_k, with MainCount computed from B_k; (5) run the existing fill pass, SecureStairs, SealEdges, CarveEmergencyExit and BuildPoints unchanged.

Keep districts apart with a deterministic cell-owner mask checked in Fits (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:85-116). Each cell's owner is its nearest root by integer distance, cells within DistrictGap of a boundary between owners are no-build, and trunk cells accept outdoor modules only. Expose the current district to Fits through a generation-time field. This one predicate is the only change inside the placement core.

Tag each FCL9ModulePlacement with int8 District (-1 for the trunk) and copy it into FCL9LevelPoint. Mix it into LayoutHash. This one field feeds the QA logs, the chunk key for ISM culling and any future per-district zone filter. No consumer needs it on day one, because hop depth already makes farther districts deeper.

Add open yards in BuildSegments, gated by the district column: emit nothing for a Door edge whose two sides are both bOutdoor, and set Door unconditionally between outdoor neighbours in OpenNeighbours. Keep the byte as Door so IsConnected keeps working.

Grid sizing: raise the 128 cap to 256, or derive it from the budget plus the district gaps. Allowing a non-square GridSize (long X for an E-W trunk) is optional, and only lines 866-871 and 889 depend on squareness. Replace the hand-copied formula at setup_stage.py:79 with a BlueprintCallable C++ static, e.g. CL9SiteLayout grid extent for (row, day scale), so the floor plane, NavBounds and the outdoor backdrop all read one source.

MapTable/site row columns needed: DistrictCount (int, 0 = off); YardShare (float, share of BaseModuleCount for the trunk, or YardModuleCount); DistrictGap (int cells, default 2; could start as a constant). SpecialCopies is reinterpreted as copies per district when DistrictCount > 0, which needs no new column, and its 1..16 clamp still fits. Zones need no change because depth stays global hops. bOpenYards is optional; tie it to DistrictCount > 0 until a site needs it separately. Add the four columns to the INHERIT list in setup_stage.py:35 and to the site.md table.
Theme: create a dedicated theme for the giant stage if any new outdoor road row is added. Otherwise filter the trunk pool by bOutdoor so it uses the existing yard_open, and add no rows to 'henhouse'.

Do not change module.md decision 3 (one entrance, one flap) silently. If K flaps are wanted for a 1 km map, ask the user and record the change in docs/decisions.md. With one grid the current CarveEmergencyExit stays valid and puts the flap at the deepest DeadEnd, which lies in the farthest district.

Tests: add CL9.Map.Districts at N=1000 (and N=2000 for the 10x gate) over 30 seeds. Assert: every seed builds; IsConnected holds; no overlap; ground floor >= 90% of budget; every district has >= 1 delivery room and >= 0.8*B_k modules; no module sits on a gap cell; district roots ordered by trunk hops have increasing median point depth; one Flap; generation ms logged per layout. Keep LargeSite and DepthBand untouched as the regression guard that DistrictCount = 0 is unchanged. Hash equality against today's values for henhouse seed 873 is the strongest check.

If the lead still prefers K independent generations for isolation, the cheaper form is 'generate K layouts, then stitch them into one FCL9SiteLayout': copy cells and edges at offsets, offset module indices, add trunk hops to district hops, and connect each gate to the trunk with a Door. That keeps every consumer single-layout. It still needs a big grid and a trunk generator, plus a 90/180-degree rotation pass for districts on the far side of the road. That makes it strictly more code than multi-root growth.
unverified: Generation time and budget fill at N=1000 and N=2000, for a single grid and for multi-root. Nothing has been measured above N=200, and CL9.Map.LargeSite logs ms per layout only at 200. TakeFrontier(bDeepest) is a linear scan per pick (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:316-327), so the spine costs O(MainCount x Frontier). It looks small on paper but has not been measured.

Whether a trunk built only from yard_open (3x3, four sockets) under deepest-first growth forms a usable road, or curls on itself. It may need an outdoor Passage row or a band mask to keep the trunk roughly E-W.
Whether a Voronoi owner mask plus DistrictGap still lets each district reach at least 90% of B_k before StallLimit (48) and the 4-pass fill run out. This needs the proposed CL9.Map.Districts test.
Real cost of the quadratic PlaceProps warning loops (CL9SiteMap.cpp:759-783) at 5x and 10x on client build time. Estimate: about 3k solid props x about 6k points, around 20M iterations. Not measured.

Whether UE 5.8 ISM components spanning 1 km get per-instance GPU culling good enough that splitting components by district or chunk is unnecessary. This needs a frame-time measurement with qa_farm_stage_pie.py on the new level.
Nav tile count and build time for a ~1.1 km NavBounds under RuntimeGeneration=Dynamic. That is outside this lens, but it constrains how large the gap and void areas between districts may be.

facts: The whole site is one transient actor. ACL9SiteMap::Find returns the first one (D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Source\CL9\World\CL9SiteMap.cpp:165-176), Rebuild reuses it (:185-219) and Clear destroys only that one (:223-230). K districts as K layouts needs either K SiteMap actors or one actor that holds K layouts.

Segment ISM components are keyed by (seg kind, mesh) across the entire layout (CL9SiteMap.cpp:400-426). Prop ISM components are keyed by (mesh, solid) (:656-683). Every segment component is BlockAll and affects navigation (:413, :421), and solid props do the same (:671-672). Each component's bounds therefore span the whole grid.

The engine gathers ISM nav geometry per tile by iterating EVERY instance of an overlapping component (ForEachInstanceMatrix with a box test, D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source\Runtime\Engine\Public\InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-166). Because the components span the whole map, nav gather cost is about tiles × total instances.

ISM registration synchronously creates one physics body per instance (CreateAllInstanceBodies / OnCreatePhysicsState, D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source\Runtime\Engine\Private\InstancedStaticMesh.cpp:2868-2896, 2909-2922). All SiteMap components are registered in one loop at the end of Build (CL9SiteMap.cpp:573-582).

The map is rebuilt synchronously in one frame on every machine. The host runs SetSiteMap -> OnRep_SiteMap -> RebuildSiteMap (D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Source\CL9\GameMode\CL9GameState.cpp:375-407), and clients run the same rebuild from OnRep. Build runs Generate, then BuildSegments, every AddInstance, PlaceProps, the lamps and registration, all in one call (CL9SiteMap.cpp:337-636).

The map is built when the lobby is entered, not when the night starts: at StartPlay (D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Source\CL9\GameMode\CL9GameMode.cpp:765-773) and at the dawn-to-lobby transition (CL9GameMode.cpp:271). The night start rebuilds only if the seed is 0 (CL9GameMode.cpp:209-212). The giant stage therefore stands through the daytime lobby, which is the worst baseline scene in performance.md (16.4 avg / 21.3 p95 ms, D:\Work\unreal\CL9\docs\systems\performance.md:31; turning VSM off saves 3.5 ms in the day lobby, performance.md:164).

Lamps are one Movable UPointLightComponent per lit prop that passes the LampDensity roll, with shadows off and volumetric scattering from the row (CL9SiteMap.cpp:789-818). MaxDrawDistance is not set, and the engine default is 0, meaning no distance cull (D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source\Runtime\Engine\Private\Components\LightComponent.cpp:499-500).

TickFlicker calls SetIntensity on every flickering lamp every frame on every machine, with no distance or visibility gate (CL9SiteMap.cpp:286-303). SetLampsOn does early-out on an unchanged value (:305-319).

The build log reports module count, instances and components (CL9SiteMap.cpp:630-634) and props (:635), but not the lamp count. The giant-stage spec's 'farm ~3,400 instances + ~650 props' figure comes from these log lines, and the QA JSON does not record them.

Monster skeletal meshes use the engine default VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = AlwaysTickPoseAndRefreshBones (D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source\Runtime\Engine\Private\Components\SkeletalMeshComponent.cpp:446) with URO off (:493). CL9 never overrides this for monsters; the only override is the player character (D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Source\CL9\Character\CL9Character.cpp:147). The only monster logic that reads a bone is the cosmetic hit puff (D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Source\CL9\Monsters\CL9Monster.cpp:403-406).

Monsters derive from ACL9ActorBase and not ACharacter (D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Source\CL9\Monsters\CL9Monster.h:72). No CL9 actor sets NetCullDistanceSquared (the project grep finds only SetNetUpdateFrequency, D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Source\CL9\Core\CL9ActorBase.cpp:9), so the engine default applies: 225,000,000, or 150 m (D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source\Runtime\Engine\Private\Actor.cpp:312).

The measured cost per monster is about 0.15 ms while chasing (5/10/20 monsters give 10.5/11.3/12.8 ms avg, and spawning 10 at once is a 98 ms spike, performance.md:177). Skeletal animation costs about 0.23 ms per monster on the game thread (performance.md:118). The CL9 game-thread budget is ≤ 4 ms at 4 players plus the maximum monster spawn (performance.md:18), but the measurement there is already 4.9 ms with 7 monsters and 1 player. ABP_Unarmed costs about 1.3 ms per player (performance.md:189).

Canonical budget: 60 fps (16.7 ms) average and p95 ≤ 25 ms in editor PIE with 1 client at night indoors (performance.md:16). The regression gate is avg +1 ms against the baseline at the same spot and viewport (performance.md:17). GPU ≤ 10 ms on a 1080p-class machine (performance.md:19). Synchronous loads at the night-start transition are allowed (measured max 38 ms, performance.md:104-105, 174). performance.md defines no hitch budget for a site build. Its baseline level is Lvl_Henhouse (performance.md:26), and no perf_probe baseline exists for Lvl_Farm.
The latest farm QA (D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Saved\QA\stage_pie_Lvl_Farm.json) reports avg_frame_ms 11.4, 22 monsters all on navmesh, and only 8 of 22 having ever moved more than 150 cm by +90 s.

qa_farm_stage_pie.py measures only the average Slate post-tick delta over the whole run, which includes night start (D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Tools\Unreal\qa_farm_stage_pie.py:93-94, 48-49). It reads only the UEDPIE_0 world (:27-31) and never moves the pawn. It samples monsters at +20/50/90 s (:97). Its nav map is hard-coded to x -10..400 m and y ±200 m (:141-143), so it cannot cover a stage about 1.1 km across. It records no p95 or max, no game/render/GPU split, no build time, no instance/component/lamp counts, no client-side numbers and no monster state histogram (state is captured only in last_positions, :155).

The render config has HWRT Lumen, VSM, ray tracing and mesh distance fields on (D:\Work\unreal\CL9\Config\DefaultEngine.ini:23-34). MegaLights is not enabled (engine default r.MegaLights.EnableForProject=0, D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source\Runtime\Renderer\Private\MegaLights\MegaLights.cpp:27). Ray-tracing instance culling defaults to mode 3 per instance with a 300 m radius (D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source\Runtime\Renderer\Private\RayTracing\RayTracingInstanceCulling.cpp:22-42), so the RT scene is already bounded by camera distance.

The navmesh is built only where the navigation system exists. Client creation is gated by bAllowClientSideNavigation (D:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Source\Runtime\NavigationSystem\Private\NavigationSystem.cpp:6541), and the project does not set it (no match in Config). Nav memory and build time therefore land on the listen host.

objections.target: Draft: 'Rendering: existing ISM-per-segment approach' (one component per (kind, mesh) across the whole stage)
objections.problem: If the current keying is kept and all districts are written into one SiteMap, every component spans about 1.1 km. Two things break before the GPU does. (1) Nav gather is tiles × total instances, because every tile overlaps every component and the helper scans all instances of each one. Going from the farm's ~2,000 tiles × ~4,000 instances to ~12,000 × ~20,000 is about 30× the work, a quadratic blow-up that the nav lens will see as 'build time' without a visible cause. (2) No component can ever be CPU-culled, measured per district or registered separately.
objections.alternative: Key the components per district: (district, kind, mesh) and (district, mesh, solid). The simplest form is one ACL9SiteMap actor per district, which also matches the 'existing generator per district' plan. Each component then overlaps only its own district's tiles, which cuts nav gather to tiles × instances-per-district (about 5×, not 30×). The cost is K times more components. Compare draw/primitive counts with stat scenerendering in the yard view before considering any finer spatial chunking.
objections.evidence: CL9SiteMap.cpp:400-426, 656-683; InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-166; farm nav '~2,000 tiles' and '~12,000+ tiles' in D:\Work\unreal\CL9\docs\goal\giant-stage.md:20

objections.target: Draft: generation/load hitch treated as 'night start on every client'
objections.problem: The build does not happen at night start. It happens at lobby entry, at StartPlay and on every dawn-to-lobby transition, and on clients when they join (OnRep). It runs in one frame: Generate, BuildSegments, about 20k AddInstance calls, about 3k props, lamp NewObject calls, then RegisterComponent for every component. Registration synchronously creates one Chaos body per instance. Every machine pays this at once, and the host also starts the dynamic nav build of the whole bounds. performance.md has no hitch budget for this. The only cited number is the henhouse night start at max 38 ms, and the farm build hitch was never measured.
objections.alternative: Measure first. Wrap Build in a scoped timer and log ms per phase (Generate / segments / props / register), and read STAT_UInstancedStaticMeshComponent_CreateAllInstanceBodies. If the 5× build exceeds what the user accepts behind the dawn screen, register one district per frame over the lobby. This is natural with one SiteMap per district. Constraint: anything that needs floor collision (physics items, monster spawns) must wait until its district is registered. The user has to set the hitch number, because performance.md has none and I will not invent one.

objections.target: Draft implicitly targets the night interior as the frame-budget scene
objections.problem: The stage stands during the daytime lobby, with the truck in the yard looking at the districts. That scene is already the worst row in the baseline (16.4 avg / 21.3 p95 ms on henhouse, at the 16.7 ms budget), and VSM costs 3.5 ms there. Five districts' walls and roofs under the sun's VSM, plus clouds and sky, is the most likely place to cross 16.7 ms first. A night-interior-only gate would miss it.
objections.alternative: Make the lobby-day yard view (at the truck, facing the districts) a mandatory perf_probe spot alongside the night interior and the night yard. If it fails, use the existing lever order in performance.md (sg.* step, then Lumen SW, ...). Do not add a bespoke culling system first.
objections.evidence: performance.md:31, 164, 157-166; CL9GameMode.cpp:271-274 (map built before the lobby, 'the stop shows tonight's destination')

objections.target: Draft: 'per-district culling by distance/visibility'
objections.problem: This is a pre-emptive optimization without a measurement (performance.md:22, 94). It also targets the wrong thing. Ray tracing is already distance-culled per instance at 300 m. Nanite/HZB handles geometry hidden behind walls, if the pieces are Nanite (unverified). Toggling a whole district's visibility does not remove its physics or nav cost. facts: Monster pathing is home-tethered, so path cost does not grow with map size. Wander picks GetRandomReachablePointInRadius(Home, max(HomeRange,200)) (Source/CL9/Monsters/CL9Monster.cpp:1130-1132). Chase gives up once the monster is more than HomeRange from home (CL9Monster.cpp:1240-1241). Return paths to HomeLocation (CL9Monster.cpp:1063-1064). Search hops use a 300 cm radius (CL9Monster.cpp:52, 628). HomeRange is 840 for chicken and pig, 1200 for raccoon and 2280 for goose (docs/plan/data/monster/chicken.md:61, raccoon.md:37, goose.md:16, pig.md:50).

Pathing is a synchronous FindPathToLocationSynchronously call after projecting both ends with a 500x500x500 extent (CL9Monster.cpp:55, 1154-1170). Chase and stalk re-path every 0.5 s (CL9Monster.cpp:49, 688-693, 892-900).

Every monster ticks every frame and has no tick interval or significance LOD (CL9Monster.cpp:71, 174-192). On the host the tick runs HostTickAI plus TickFootstep. TickHitFlash, TickHitFeel and TickStateSounds run on every machine.

SenseTick loops over characters only (four or fewer). It traces line of sight only when the character is within SightRange, so far monsters cost no traces (CL9Monster.cpp:960-971, 1012-1016). The asleep wake check loops over characters only (CL9Monster.cpp:501-514).

Moving monsters do a swept AddActorWorldOffset plus SetActorRotation every tick (CL9Monster.cpp:1195-1198). The root sphere overlaps all channels except WorldStatic (blocked) and Camera (ignored) (CL9Monster.cpp:77-83). WaypointTolerance is 25 cm (CL9Monster.cpp:39).

The O(N) monster loops (kill alarm, pack alarm, execute anchor) run per event, not per tick (CL9Monster.cpp:1541-1573, 1640-1651, 1868-1879). TryBeginExecute is gated by ExecuteRadius before the sweep (CL9Monster.cpp:1905-1911).

The monster mesh keeps the engine default VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = AlwaysTickPoseAndRefreshBones (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Components/SkeletalMeshComponent.cpp:446). Only the player overrides it (Source/CL9/Character/CL9Character.cpp:147). So the host animates every monster, seen or not.

Measured costs: monster skeletal animation is the largest single game-thread item at about 0.23 ms per monster (docs/systems/performance.md:118-119). Chase with 5, 10 and 20 monsters measured 10.5, 11.3 and 12.8 ms, about 0.15 ms per monster. Spawning 10 monsters at once took 98 ms (performance.md:177). Budgets are 16.7 ms per frame and 4 ms or less of CL9 game-thread code with 4 players and the maximum monster spawn (performance.md:16-18).

Monsters replicate movement at 20 Hz (Source/CL9/Core/CL9ActorBase.cpp:8-9, CL9Monster.cpp:72). They keep the engine NetCullDistanceSquared of 225000000, which is 150 m (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Actor.cpp:312). Clients run no AI (CL9Monster.cpp:184-192). On re-entering relevancy, a client runs LoadData again (SetSkeletalMesh and SetAnimInstanceClass, CL9Monster.cpp:120-167).
All monsters spawn synchronously in StartNight right after the clock starts (Source/CL9/GameMode/CL9GameMode.cpp:214-223, 544-565). Nothing spawns later in the night.

The site map, and so the dynamic navmesh build, is made in the lobby, not at night: at StartPlay (CL9GameMode.cpp:768-773) and on every return to the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:270-271). The night falls back to building one only if there is no seed (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212). Nothing gates night start on navigation finishing.

Project navigation config sets only RuntimeGeneration=Dynamic (Config/DefaultEngine.ini:85-86). Engine defaults are TileSizeUU=1000 and CellSize=19 (UE_5.8 Engine/Config/BaseEngine.ini:3052-3053), with invokers off (bGenerateNavigationOnlyAroundNavigationInvokers=false at NavigationSystem.cpp:936). Clients create a navigation system only when bAllowClientSideNavigation is set (NavigationSystem.cpp:6541), and the project does not set it.

Farm navigation today: NavBounds is stretched to 465 x 440 m, which is about 2,070 tiles at 10 m. The runtime build finishes within about 20 s (docs/systems/map.md:191-195). The QA nav_map in Saved/QA/stage_pie_Lvl_Farm.json is 41x42 cells at 10 m and all '#', so empty ground inside the bounds is navmeshed too. setup_stage.py sizes one box per level and deletes the saved RecastNavMesh (Tools/Unreal/setup_stage.py:159-196).

Recast tile capacity is summed over every inclusion bounds box, so several NavMeshBoundsVolumes are supported (UE_5.8 RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5133-5163, 5748-5773). The hard-limit error says to use bigger tiles or raise TileNumberHardLimit (RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5768-5772).

ISM navigation export scans every instance of the component on each per-tile query (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Public/InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-167). CL9SiteMap builds one ISM per (seg kind, mesh) and one per (prop mesh, solid) across the whole site, all nav-relevant (Source/CL9/World/CL9SiteMap.cpp:405-425, 656-683). Instances are added before RegisterComponent (CL9SiteMap.cpp:504-581), so registration happens once per component.

Movable nav-relevant things dirty the dynamic navmesh at runtime: promoted carts block Pawn (Source/CL9/Items/CL9Item.cpp:558-565, and PrimitiveComponent.cpp:3684-3686 makes Pawn-blocking components nav-relevant), and the CL9FlapIn body affects navigation (Source/CL9/World/CL9FlapIn.cpp:25).

ACL9SiteMap::Find returns the first site map (CL9SiteMap.cpp:165-176). The night spawner reads points and depth bands from that single layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-515, 600-613). The generator span cap is clamp(ceil(sqrt(N*6))*2, 16, 128) (Source/CL9/World/CL9SiteLayout.cpp:866).

The farm QA records only +20, +50 and +90 s samples after cl9.night (Tools/Unreal/qa_farm_stage_pie.py:96-122). The last run had 22 monsters, all on the navmesh, but only 8 ever moved more than 150 cm by +90 s, with a frame average of 11.4 ms (Saved/QA/stage_pie_Lvl_Farm.json). So today's 'all active' baseline is mostly idle or asleep monsters.

Lethal Company code defaults for power caps are indoor 8, outdoor 15 and daytime 20 (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-monsters.md:403-407). Measured moon values (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-map.md:192-207): Titan size 2.2 with indoor 18, outdoor 7, daytime 20. Artifice is 1.8 with 13/13/15. Liquidation is 1.6 with 13/13/20. March is 1.75 with 14/12/14. Rend and Dine are 1.8 with 10 indoor. Experimentation is 1.0 with 4/8/5. Embrion's outdoor 70 is an outlier.

Lethal per-enemy power and caps (lethal-monsters.md:595-629): indoor enemies cost 1-3 power, for example Hoarding bug, Nutcracker and Masked at 1 with max 10, and Flowerman, Crawler and Jester at 3. Outdoor: MouthDog 2 (max 8), ForestGiant 3 (max 3), Baboon hawk 0.5 (max 15).

Lethal spawns ramp over the day. Nothing spawns until currentDayTime > 85 of totalTime 700. Batches come every 2 in-game hours, each clamped to at most 20 and to free vents. Kills refund power (lethal-monsters.md:449-462, 543-563, 387-389). Every enemy 'thinks' on AIIntervalTime 0.2 s, about 5 Hz, with no distance sleep (lethal-monsters.md:53-63).

CL9 farm counts: the zone base sums are 34-45 monsters (Tools/Unreal/stages/farm.json:26-28). MonsterCountCurve runs 0.6 on day 1, 1.0 on day 5 and 1.5 on day 10 (docs/plan/data/progression.md:29). That gives 20-27 on day 1 (25 observed, map.md:194) and 51-68 on day 10.

objections.target: Nav: 'dynamic navmesh over all districts + yard' (one whole-bounds box as today)
objections.problem: A single box around ~1.1 km at 5x is about 12-13k tiles at the default 10 m tile, and about 25k at 10x. Even if build time is linear from the farm's ~2,070 tiles in under 20 s, that is about 2 min at 5x and about 4 min at 10x. The build runs in the lobby, which has no minimum length, and nothing stops the night from starting before navigation is done. Monsters standing on unbuilt tiles then keep failing projection and stay put, retrying StartNewWander every 0.5 s. Yards and gaps between districts get navmesh that no monster can use, because every monster is tethered to its home.
objections.alternative: Give the stage fixed district slots: each district's position and footprint is set in the stage JSON and the seed only fills its contents. setup_stage.py then places one NavMeshBoundsVolume per slot, sized to that slot's day-10 span plus a HomeRange margin of about 25 m. Leave yards without navmesh until a yard monster exists. Tile capacity sums per volume, so several volumes are supported. Add a host gate so the truck cannot leave for the night while UNavigationSystemV1 reports a build in progress, or measure and enforce a minimum lobby time.

objections.target: Nav: navigation invokers on monsters to satisfy 'always active'
objections.problem: It satisfies the rule only on paper. Invokers register when monsters spawn, and monsters spawn at StartNight, so the navmesh build moves from the hidden lobby into the first seconds or minutes of the night, and every monster is frozen until its tiles exist. The invoker flag is NavigationSystem-wide (default false), so it changes henhouse, farm and pigfarm too. Spawn points cover the whole layout, so invoker discs around ~50-100 home-tethered monsters cover almost all of each district anyway. The only gain is leaving yards without navmesh, which per-district bounds already give, deterministically and in the lobby.
objections.alternative: Do not use invokers. Use per-district bounds volumes as above. If invokers are ever wanted, put them on fixed per-district anchor actors that exist from the lobby, not on monsters.
objections.evidence: NavigationSystem.cpp:936, 5437; CL9GameMode.cpp:214-223; CL9GameMode.cpp:519-541 (spawn points span the layout)

objections.target: Rendering/nav: 'existing ISM-per-segment approach' carried to districts
objections.problem: Recast's per-tile export of an ISM component scans every instance of that component on each tile query. CL9SiteMap makes one ISM per (kind, mesh) for the whole site. If districts are built as one SiteMap actor, or share the ComponentFor maps, gathering costs tiles x instances. That is about 13k x 17k, roughly 221M bounds tests at 5x, against about 7M on the farm (30x worse), and about 120x worse at 10x. It is quadratic, not linear.
objections.alternative: Make the design say it explicitly: each district is its own ACL9SiteMap actor with its own ISM component set, or ISMs are chunked per sector of about 100 m. Each tile then scans only that district's instances and the cost stays at the farm's level times K. Note that ACL9SiteMap::Find and the night spawner assume a single map and must loop over all of them.

objections.target: Nav: 'larger tiles' as the tile-count fix
objections.problem: A 20 m tile cuts the tile count by 4x, but voxelisation work per tile grows about 4x, so total rasterisation stays roughly the same. The real gain is per-tile overhead and the ISM scan count, which per-district components already fix. The cost is that every runtime dirty area, such as a cart moving or a flap opening, rebuilds a 400 m² tile instead of a 100 m² one.
objections.alternative: Keep TileSizeUU 1000 as the default. Measure 1000 against 2000 at 5x only after per-district ISM components and per-district bounds are in place, and pick a size from the measured build time and cart-push rebuild cost.

objections.target: Draft says nothing about the always-on per-monster cost on the host
objections.problem: The host animates every monster whether it is visible or not, because the engine default AlwaysTickPoseAndRefreshBones is never overridden for monsters. At about 0.15-0.23 ms per monster, 80 monsters cost about 12-18 ms and 100 monsters about 15-23 ms of game thread. That blows both the 16.7 ms frame target and the 4 ms CL9 budget before AI is counted. Today's farm number (11.4 ms with 22 monsters) hides this because only 8 of the 22 ever moved.
objections.alternative: Split 'active' into behaviour and presentation. AI, movement and senses always run, per the user's decision. The monster MeshComponent uses OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered, or OnlyTickPoseWhenRendered, plus update-rate optimisation. Hits use the root sphere and the execute camera only matters when someone is close, so gameplay does not depend on unseen bones. Optionally, also lower the think rate when no player is within about 50 m, matching Lethal's 0.2 s AIIntervalTime, which applies to all of its enemies. If so, clamp the movement step so it does not overshoot the 25 cm WaypointTolerance.

objections.target: Population spawn timing (unchanged StartNight bulk spawn)
objections.problem: Every monster spawns in one frame in StartNight. The measured cost was 98 ms for 10 monsters at once, so 45-80 monsters means roughly a 0.45-0.8 s host hitch at the moment the night starts.
objections.alternative: Spread spawning over frames, for example a few per frame per district during the first 1-2 s. Or adopt a Lethal-style ramp in which far districts fill in batches over the night. A ramp does not conflict with 'never sleep or despawn by distance'.

objections.target: Population count ('sensible by comparison with Lethal')
objections.problem: Scaling the farm by 5x gives 100-135 monsters on day 1 and 255-340 on day 10, which is not workable on the host. The farm on day 10 (51-68) is already 2-3x Lethal's largest-moon peak for a single facility. Titan allows 18 indoor plus 7 outdoor power, which is about 9-15 indoor and 2-14 outdoor enemies at 1-3 power each, about 12-25 concurrent, reached only late in the day.
objections.alternative: Treat each district (about 200 modules, about a 1-minute spine like one Lethal facility) as one Lethal-moon equivalent and give it a power budget. Suggested CL9 powers: chicken and sheep 1, goose and raccoon 2, pig 3. Per district, day 1 runs from 6 power (near) to 12 power (far), which spans Lethal's Experimentation 4 to Rend 10. Day 10 runs from 12 to 18, which is Titan. At 5x that is about 45 monsters on day 1 (near 5, two mid at 8, two far at 12), about 65 on day 5, and a hard cap of about 80 on day 10. Count is capped by power the way Lethal does it, and the day curve shifts the species mix once the cap is reached. 10x keeps the same per-district budget, about 90 on day 1 and 160 on day 10, and only proceeds if 5x holds its frame budget with 80 monsters all awake.

objections.target: QA plan: 'qa_farm_stage_pie.py and layout tests at the new size'
objections.problem: The script starts timing at cl9.night and samples only at +20, +50 and +90 s. It never measures how long navigation takes after SetSiteMap, or the worst case where the night starts at once. The 500-unit projection extent passes a monster whose own tile is missing as long as a neighbouring tile exists. It also does not force monsters awake, so the 'always active' cost goes untested.
objections.alternative: Add these to the giant QA. Record seconds from SetSiteMap until IsNavigationBeingBuilt is false, along with tile count and navmesh memory. Run a night started immediately after the lobby build. Project with a small extent, about 100 units. Run a pass with every monster forced awake and wandering through a cheat, and record host game-thread ms with stat dumpframe. Add a scripted walk across yards to see client relevancy churn.

objections.target: Replication at district scale (not addressed in the draft)

Each re-entry runs LoadData, which sets the skeletal mesh and the ABP. This keeps client CPU bounded, which is good, but the churn cost and any hitch have not been measured.
objections.alternative: Keep the default cull distance and do not make monsters always relevant. Measure re-entry hitches in the yard-walk QA. Only if hitches show up, pool the anim instance or tune NetCullDistance per species.

Districts must be separate ACL9SiteMap actors, or at least separate ISM component sets, so Recast's per-tile ISM instance scan stays local to a district. State this in the spec and update ACL9SiteMap::Find and SpawnNightPopulation to loop over all districts.

Gate night start on navigation completion on the host (no build in progress), and show 'preparing' in the lobby if needed. The giant QA records time from map build to navigation done.

If the host is still over budget after animation culling, add think-rate LOD (for example 5-10 Hz when no player is within about 50 m) with a clamped movement step, citing Lethal's 0.2 s AIIntervalTime as precedent that this still counts as 'always active'.

Day 10 has a hard cap of about 80 (12-18 power per district, Titan). The day curve shifts the species mix once the cap is reached. 10x doubles the district count at the same per-district budget, and only after 5x passes with 80 monsters awake on the host.

facts: Movement speeds: WalkSpeed 396 cm/s, RunSpeed 654 cm/s, sustained empty-handed run/walk cycle 506.6 cm/s (docs/plan/economy.md:123); a cart moves at 297 cm/s (economy.md:135). The carrying slowdown f(weight) is still undecided (economy.md:125-126). The lead's 4.6 m/s figure sits between walking and the sustained cycle; I use 4.5 m/s below.

Night-length rule of thumb: night ≈ 160 + 5.3 × spine modules, where spine = BaseModuleCount × MainPathShare. It is fitted to only two points (henhouse 16/245 s, farm 60/480 s) and is described as a starting value to be tuned by play (docs/systems/stage.md:58-59).

SiteSizeCurve multiplies the module count from 0.85 on day 1 to 1.25 on day 10, while NightLengthCurve stays flat (docs/plan/data/progression.md:34-35). setup_stage.py already sizes the ground and NavBounds for the day-10 grid (Tools/Unreal/setup_stage.py:40-41,150-151).

Grid span is Clamp(ceil(sqrt(6N))*2, 16, 128) cells, at CL9SiteLayout.cpp:866 and mirrored in Python at setup_stage.py:79. A 200-module district is 70 cells (350 m) wide on day 1 and 78 cells (390 m) on day 10, because CellSize is 500 (docs/systems/asset-swap.md:252). Layout.Origin = (EntryOffset, -Span*Cell/2) (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:871), so the gate is on the west edge, centred.

Each Generate() call already carves its own entrance door (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:906-908) and one one-way flap exit at the deepest dead end (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:423-471, 969; module.md:190-195, the Lethal fire-exit analogue). A per-district gate and exit therefore come free with one layout per district.
Depth for Zones is normalised against the farthest hop in that one layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217). With one layout per district, zones are automatically evaluated per district.

Jars are placed one per delivery module of the layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:615-646). SpecialCopies applies per layout (CL9SiteMap.cpp:363). Depositing in a jar banks the item without walking it to the truck, and each deposit brings the blackout 4 s closer (docs/systems/raiding.md:26-27; docs/plan/data/rules.md:58).

Players still have to walk back to the truck: at dawn, any equipment item farther than EquipmentKeepRadius from the truck pad is destroyed, including items held by players (CL9GameMode.cpp:1149-1191, 1182-1186).

ACL9SiteMap is a singleton in practice. Find returns the first actor (CL9SiteMap.cpp:165-176), Rebuild and Clear act on that one (CL9SiteMap.cpp:178-230), and SpawnNight reads one SiteMap's layout and points (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-646). Other callers are GameState::RebuildSiteMap (CL9GameState.cpp:393-407) and the cheat LayEditorSiteMap (CL9Cheats.cpp:37-73).

SiteToWorld ignores actor rotation: it returns GetActorLocation()+(Local.X,Local.Y,0) (CL9SiteMap.cpp:238-242). The flap is spawned at GetActorLocation()+Spot with zero rotation (CL9SiteMap.cpp:465). ISM instances are added in local space (CL9SiteMap.cpp:504,549,567,786), so meshes would follow a yawed actor, but points and flaps would not.

The map is laid during the lobby, before the night starts (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212, 270-271), and at StartPlay (CL9GameMode.cpp:764-773). StartNight does not wait for the navmesh to finish building. The only nav setting in config is RuntimeGeneration=Dynamic (Config/DefaultEngine.ini:85-86).

Monsters are leashed to where they spawned: they wander inside HomeRange (CL9Monster.cpp:1123-1132), and chase breaks when they leave it (CL9Monster.cpp:1240-1241). HomeRange is 840 cm for chicken and pig, 1200 for raccoon and 2280 for goose (docs/plan/data/monster/*.md). Monsters never cross a yard, so monsters in unvisited districts never affect play.

Monsters do not set VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption; only the player character does (CL9Character.cpp:147). Performance budget is ≤ 4 ms of CL9 game-thread time (docs/systems/performance.md:18). Measured: 7 monster skeletal meshes ≈ 1.6 ms (performance.md:40). Each monster does one sight trace per player per frame (performance.md:118).

Farm zones total 34-45 monsters at base (Tools/Unreal/stages/farm.json:26-28) × MonsterCountCurve (0.6 on day 1 → 1.5 on day 10; progression.md:29). That gives about 25 on day 1 and about 60 on day 10.

Lethal Company comparison: indoor power caps run from 4 to 18 per moon and outdoor from 6 to 15 (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-map.md:195-206). Each creature costs 0.5-3 power (lethal-monsters.md:597-629). A day is totalTime 700 with startingGlobalTime 100, so about 600 s remain after landing (lethal-map.md:503-505).

Orders ask for about 2 orders of 1-3 cooked items per day (docs/plan/data/order.md:51-52, 89-91). The farm already spawns 40-50 eggs and 22-28 meat at base (farm.json:26-28), so what one night earns is limited by walking and carrying time, not by how many items spawn.

CL9.Map.LargeSite tests ModuleCount 200 over 30 seeds. It checks build, connectivity, overlap, one exit, at least 2 deliveries and at least 90% of the ground budget, and it logs ms per layout (CL9SiteLayoutTests.cpp:541-617). It does not test the day-10 count (250), the occupied bounding box, or spine length in metres.

objections.target: Equal 5 × ~200 module districts
objections.problem: This does not fit the 600 s walk budget for every district. The project's own formula gives one district a yard round-trip allowance of 600 - (160 + 5.3·0.3·N). For N = 200 that leaves 122 s by the base count (one-way yard of about 275 m at 4.5 m/s), and only 43 s on day 10, when 250 modules mean a spine of 75 (one-way yard of about 97 m). The grids are 390 m square on day 10, and with 90° yaw only two districts can sit right next to the truck (east and west arms, about 10 m). The north and south arms must be at least half a span away (about 195 m), and a fifth district at least about 300 m. So at least one equal 200-module district cannot be raided to its deep zone, and the far districts fail on day 10. The players' choice collapses to 'the nearest one'.
objections.alternative: Size each district by its yard distance. Per district: N_max ≈ (440 − 0.444·L)/1.59 by base count, where L is the one-way gate distance in metres (L=10→274, 100→249, 200→221, 300→193, 400→165), and divide by 1.25 for the day-10 worst case. Example totalling about 1,000: east and west arms about 230 each (L≈10-30 m), north and south arms about 190 (L≈195 m), one corner district about 160 (L≈300 m). Bigger near the truck, smaller further away.

objections.target: 'Districts further from the truck are the more dangerous/valuable ones'
objections.problem: If 'further' also means as big and as deep, the far deep zone, which holds the killers and most of the meat, cannot be reached and left again inside 600 s. The draft sets distance against depth when they compete for the same budget. Depth normalisation is per layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217), so a far district's 'deep' zone is only as deep as that district itself.
objections.alternative: Make far districts small and dense rather than big. Danger and value come from the zone composition (more pig, raccoon and meat rows) in a short-spine district. Data needed: an optional Zones override per district entry (empty means use the site Zones). A cheaper variant is one float per district (DepthBias) that shifts that district's points into the existing middle and deep bands. ValueRate stays at 1.0 because the economy is out of scope (stage.md:55).

objections.target: Arranging districts 'around/along an outdoor yard' without saying how they are oriented
objections.problem: The code cannot orient a district today. SiteToWorld drops actor rotation (CL9SiteMap.cpp:238-242) and the flap spawns unrotated (CL9SiteMap.cpp:465), so every gate faces west (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:871,889). With yaw 0 only, the districts have to stack in a north-south column 280-390 m apart. Gates 400-600 m away allow only about 100-170 modules, and the total falls well short of 1,000 (about 600-650 with 3 districts).
objections.alternative: Support yaw in multiples of 90° only, and treat it as required, not polish. Fix SiteToWorld to use GetActorTransform().TransformPosition, and spawn the flap with the actor's rotation; ISMs are already local and follow the actor. Lay districts out as a cross centred on the truck pad. Before placing the west arm, check where the existing food truck, kitchen and counter props sit in the duplicated level.

objections.target: 'Nav: open question whether tile count/build time needs navigation invokers or larger tiles'
objections.problem: Invokers are close to incompatible with decision 4 unless every monster carries one. They are also unnecessary: the map is built in the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212, 270-271), so the dynamic nav already gets the whole lobby to build. The real gap is that StartNight never waits for the nav to finish, so on a short first lobby after StartPlay (CL9GameMode.cpp:773) monsters would spawn onto missing tiles.
objections.alternative: Build full dynamic nav over the union of districts with no invokers and no tile change. Gate StartNight, or at least log a warning, while UNavigationSystemV1::IsNavigationBuildInProgress() is true. Change tile size only if the measured build time is longer than a normal lobby.

objections.target: 'Rendering: per-district culling by distance/visibility; lamp count scales with districts'
objections.problem: One SiteMap actor per district already gives per-district ISM components, and the engine's frustum and occlusion culling then works per district at no cost. A new culling system is scope with no measurement behind it. The cost the draft misses is monster animation: all monsters stay active (decision 4), and 7 skeletal meshes already cost about 1.6 ms (performance.md:40). Around 100 monsters would break the 4 ms game-thread budget (performance.md:18) even though most are off-screen.
objections.alternative: Add no culling system in the first cut. Give monsters VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered (or similar): AI, perception and movement keep running, which honours decision 4, and only off-screen pose evaluation is skipped. Measure lamps per district at 5×, and only then consider a per-district LampDensity.
objections.evidence: CL9Character.cpp:147 (only the player sets it); no monster setting found in Source/CL9/Monsters

objections.target: Monster count left as 'sensible vs Lethal' without a number (and the implicit 5 × farm)
objections.problem: Five times the farm is about 125 monsters on day 1 and about 300 on day 10, all active, and leashed (HomeRange 8-23 m) inside districts nobody visits. That is pure cost with no effect on play. The farm is already denser than Lethal: Lethal's whole interior holds at most 18 power (lethal-map.md:204), and creatures cost 1-3 power each.
objections.alternative: Treat one district as one Lethal interior, which fits because each district has one entrance and one fire exit (module.md:190-195). Give each district about 10-14 monsters at base, which is about 6-8 on day 1 and 15-21 on day 10. Total for 5 districts: about 35-40 on day 1 and about 90-100 on day 10. Near districts get lighter rows, far ones heavier. Treat the day-10 total as a ceiling to be checked against the measured game-thread time, not as a target.

objections.target: Yards as plain walking space
objections.problem: Monsters are leashed and the yard has no LevelPoints, so the yard has no content: every metre of it is dead, risk-free walking. The cart is worse at 2.97 m/s (economy.md:135), roughly 1.5 times the yard time. Equipment must come back to the truck or be lost (CL9GameMode.cpp:1182-1186), so players cross the yard twice.
objections.alternative: In the first cut, keep yards short; do not try to make them interesting. Place districts using the day-10 span plus a small road gap (about 10-20 m), and check each L_i against the formula above. Yard monsters or loot need a new spawn source (the flat-site ring at CL9GameMode.cpp:555 only applies when there is no generator), so leave them for later if playtests show the yard is boring.

objections.target: 'New MapTable row + level; QA ... and layout automation tests at the new size'
objections.problem: The generator is untouched, so a layout test 'at the new size' (1,000 modules) tests nothing new. What is new, and untested, is how districts are placed (overlap, yard distances) and whether a 230-module (day 10: about 290) district still fills to 90%. LargeSite only covers 200 (CL9SiteLayoutTests.cpp:551).
objections.alternative: Add one placement test: for the stage row, no two districts' day-10 grid rectangles overlap, and each gate's L_i satisfies the size rule. Run LargeSite at the largest district's day-10 count. Add AddInfo lines for the occupied bounding box (how much of the span the building actually covers) and spine length in metres, both computed from Modules with no PIE.

objections.target: Separate items needed for 'SpecialCopies per district', 'own yard_gate per district' and 'depth zones per district'
objections.problem: All three already happen for every layout: SpecialCopies at CL9SiteMap.cpp:363, the gate and flap at CL9SiteLayout.cpp:906-908,969, and depth normalisation at CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217. Listing them as design work makes the scope look bigger than it is.
objections.alternative: Drop them from the task list and note that they come for free with one layout per district.

recommendations: Smallest implementation that meets all five decisions: (1) Add UCL9SiteDef.Districts = array of {Offset2D cm from the truck pad, Yaw ∈ {0,90,180,270}, ModuleCount, optional Zones override}. An empty array behaves as today, so henhouse, farm and pigfarm are untouched. (2) Spawn one ACL9SiteMap per district with sub-seed = hash(seed, index); turn Find, Rebuild and Clear into loops (CL9SiteMap.cpp:165-230, CL9GameState.cpp:393-407, CL9Cheats.cpp:37-73). (3) Make SiteToWorld and the flap spawn rotation-aware (CL9SiteMap.cpp:238-242,465). (4) Wrap the existing SpawnNight point/zone/jar block (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-646) in a loop over the SiteMaps. (5) Change setup_stage.py grid_extent to the union of district rectangles at day-10 span, with ground and NavBounds sized to that union (setup_stage.py:77-82,150-151). (6) Set off-screen anim ticking on monsters. (7) Gate StartNight on nav build finished. Out of the first cut: no change to the generator or its 128 cap, no invokers, no tile change, no HLOD or culling system, no yard content, no economy change.

Size each district by the walk budget, not equally: N_i ≤ (440 − 0.444·L_i)/1.59 by base count (divide by 1.25 to also hold on day 10). Suggested 5-district cross: east and west arms about 230 each next to the truck, north and south about 190 at roughly half a span, one corner about 160. That is about 1,000 base modules, with a bigger district nearer the truck and a smaller, denser and more dangerous one further out.

Monster total: about 10-14 at base per district (one district ≈ one Lethal interior, whose cap is ≤ 18 power), which is about 35-40 on day 1 and about 90-100 on day 10 for 5 districts. Accept that number only after a scripted PIE frame-time capture at day-10 counts on the host with 4 players.

Items: keep the farm's density per district module (about 0.33 per module at base) and leave ValueRate at 1.0. Income stays bounded by what a team can bank from about one district per night, so the economy does not change. Flag a balance check rather than redesigning.

Night clock for the row: NightLength 600; DarkBase and DarkMin scaled in proportion to the farm (480→360/240), i.e. about 450/300. Note that DarkAccel (4 s per deposit) brings the blackout forward faster on nights with many deposits.

Before fixing district offsets, measure: (a) the occupied bounding box as a share of the span at 150-290 modules; if the building only fills about 60% of the span from the gate, districts can be packed closer and every L_i shrinks; (b) spine path length in metres per district; (c) a scripted PIE walk from truck to gate to the deepest point to the nearest jar and back to the truck at day-10 size, to check the 160 + 5.3·S formula, which comes from only two data points.
Raise as an open question for the user, without assuming an answer: how do players tell districts apart when choosing (signage, lobby map, nothing)? Without that, 'choose a district' is a blind pick.
unverified: The walk time per spine module. giant-stage.md:22 says 'about 1 min for 60 modules', but this is an estimate, not a measurement, and the 5.3 s/module slope comes from only two stages.
How much of its 390 m span a 200-250 module district's building actually covers. This decides the minimum spacing between districts and every yard distance L.

Nav build time for the union of districts (about 6,000-6,500 tiles for an 800 m cross, if TileSizeUU is the 1000 cm default, which is not set in DefaultEngine.ini) compared with a typical lobby length, especially the first night after StartPlay.
Game-thread cost of about 90-100 always-active monsters with off-screen animation skipped: sight traces (1 per player per frame) plus pathing (performance.md:118).
Whether the food truck, kitchen and counter in the duplicated Lvl_Henhouse lie west of the truck pad and would collide with a district at yaw 180 on the west arm.
Cost of point lights at 5× LampDensity coverage, and whether far district lamps are distance-culled.
Generation time per 200-250 module layout × 5 on every client. LargeSite logs ms per layout, but I have not read a recorded value.

Client-side cost of replicating monsters in districts the players are not in. I did not find a NetCullDistance or bAlwaysRelevant override in Source/CL9, so I assume the default relevancy distance applies.

decisions.decision: Architecture: K districts, each a separate ACL9SiteMap actor that runs the UNCHANGED generator (CL9SiteLayout::Generate) on its own sub-seed, module count and world transform. Add FCL9SiteDistrict {Offset (cm from the truck pad), Yaw in {0,90,180,270}, ModuleCount (base), Zones (empty = use the site Zones)} and TArray<FCL9SiteDistrict> Districts on UCL9SiteDef. When Districts is empty, the current single-site path runs byte-identical, so henhouse, farm and pigfarm do not change.
decisions.rationale: There are few consumers, and I verified each one: GameMode::SpawnNight (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-646), GameState Rebuild/Clear (CL9GameState.cpp:401,405) and Cheats (CL9Cheats.cpp:46,73). Each turns into a loop. With one actor per district, ISM components are per district for free (CL9SiteMap.cpp:400-426, 656-683). That bounds the per-tile instance scan in Recast's nav gather (verified at InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-167) and the quadratic PlaceProps warning loop (CL9SiteMap.cpp:759-783) to farm scale times K. The 200-module behaviour proven by CL9.Map.LargeSite stays valid, and the 128 cap is never approached.
decisions.rejected: Generator lens: multi-root growth in one grid. It needs changes to the placement core (owner mask in Fits, trunk phase, MainCount from the budget at cpp:540, per-district Specials at cpp:554-572, open-yard rules in BuildSegments). Nobody has measured it at N >= 1000. It would still need district-keyed ISM components to fix the nav gather. It is strictly more code and risk than looping 5 consumers. Also rejected: a 'stitch K layouts into one' variant, which needs the same rotation work plus a trunk generator.

decisions.decision: Grid cap row: keep the cap at 128 and do not touch it. The largest district at day 10 is 230 x 1.25 = 288 modules, which gives Span = ceil(sqrt(1728))*2 = 84 cells.
decisions.rationale: Under the district design no layout comes near 128. The generator lens is right that raising the cap would be harmless, but nothing needs it, so it is not done.
decisions.rejected: Raising the cap to 256 or deriving it from the budget (only needed for the single-grid design).

decisions.decision: Generation row: every machine generates K layouts from sub-seeds derived from the one replicated seed: SubSeed_i = HashCombine(Seed, i), with 0 remapped to 1, because Seed 0 builds nothing (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:842). Log LayoutHash and build ms per district. Add a scoped per-phase timer to ACL9SiteMap::Build (Generate / segments / props+lamps / register). Keep the synchronous build. The fallback, if the measured build hitch is over the budget the user sets (see unresolved), is to build one district per frame during the lobby.
decisions.rationale: Only one seed is replicated (CL9GameState.cpp:382-407). Sub-seeds keep determinism with no new replication. The build runs at lobby entry, not at night start (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212, 270-271, 765-773). The panel verified this, which corrects the draft.
decisions.rejected: Async or streamed generation before anyone has measured a single-frame build.

decisions.decision: District rotation: support Yaw in multiples of 90 degrees by spawning each district actor with its yaw. Change SiteToWorld to GetActorTransform().TransformPosition (CL9SiteMap.cpp:238-242). Spawn the flap with the actor's rotation and pass it the world-rotated Outward (CL9SiteMap.cpp:465-468). Nothing else needs to change: all ISM instances are local (AddInstance bWorldSpace=false at CL9SiteMap.cpp:504, 549, 567, 786), components and lamps are attached to the root (:422, :679, :802), and night spawns use random yaw, with jars at a zero rotator.
decisions.rationale: Without yaw every gate faces west (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:889, 906-908). Districts would then stack in one N-S column, the yard distances L reach 400-600 m, and 1,000 modules cannot fit the 600 s walk budget. Rotation lets the districts sit as a cross around the truck.
decisions.rejected: A whole-layout rotation pass inside the generator (generator lens). Actor yaw does the same thing with two small edits.

decisions.decision: District count, size and placement: 5 districts on fixed slots in the stage JSON, with the seed filling only their contents. Initial slots: East (yaw 0) and West (yaw 180) at about 230 base modules each with gates at L of about 10-30 m; North and South (yaw 90/270) at about 190 each with L of about 210 m; one far district at about 160 with L of about 300 m. That sums to about 1,000 base modules (user decision 1). Size rule per district, from stage.md:58-59 with NightLength 600 and MainPathShare 0.30: 1.59*N_i + 0.444*L_i <= 440 (one-way yard distance L in metres at 4.5 m/s). Slots may not overlap as rotated day-10 span rectangles. Final offsets are set after the footprint measurement.
decisions.rationale: The project applies the night formula at base count; farm is 480 s at base 200 and gets no day-10 correction, because NightLengthCurve is flat. Every district can then be raided to its deep zone and back within one night, while all five clearly cannot (user decisions 2 and 3). Near districts are larger and far ones smaller and denser. Fixed slots satisfy both the nav lens (deterministic bounds) and the play lens (walk budget).
decisions.rejected: Equal 5 x 200 districts: N/S and far districts would break the 600 s budget. The play lens example also misstated that its sizes hold on day 10 (230 at L=10 gives 1.99*230 > 440). The project convention is base count, so the sizes are kept but applied at base.

decisions.decision: Truck and yard: one truck pad, the existing ACL9TruckPad, at the yard centre. It anchors every district actor (pad + rotated offset). The yard is the level's bare floor plane, scaled by setup_stage.py to the union of rotated day-10 district rectangles plus MARGIN. There are no generated yard modules, no yard content and no yard monsters in the first cut.
decisions.rationale: This is the smallest change. setup_stage already scales the Floor/Ground actors (setup_stage.py:169-196). A generated yard would add fenced paddocks (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1072-1113) or a large Grid instance count for nothing. Monsters are leashed to HomeRange (CL9Monster.cpp:1130-1132, 1240-1241), so an empty yard costs no AI.
decisions.rejected: Yards made of yard_open modules, open-yard segment rules and a new road row in the 'henhouse' theme, which would change the henhouse/farm/pigfarm pools.

decisions.decision: Entrances and exits: each district keeps the generator's own yard_gate (Start, facing the truck after yaw) and its own single flapIn at its deepest dead end. Record in docs/decisions.md that module.md decision 3 ('one entrance, one flap') applies per district building, and that the truck docks at the stage pad rather than at each gate.
decisions.rationale: User decision 3 makes districts separate building clusters, and each one has to be enterable. One entrance plus one fire exit per building matches the Lethal-interior analogue that module.md:193-195 cites. It costs no code, because the generator already does it per layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:906-908, 969), and the four one-flap test assertions stay valid per layout.
decisions.rejected: One entrance and one flap for the whole stage. Only the single-grid design can express that, and it makes the far districts reachable only through the near ones.

decisions.decision: Depth zones: depth is evaluated per district (per-layout hop normalisation, CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217, unchanged). Districts differ through an optional per-district Zones override (reusing FCL9SiteZone); an empty override uses the site Zones. Far districts get heavier rows (more pig, raccoon and meat). ValueRate stays 1.0.
decisions.rationale: This answers the generator lens objection that per-district normalisation makes every district identical. It reuses the existing struct and the existing SpawnNight zone loop (CL9GameMode.cpp:600-613), called once per district.
decisions.rejected: Global hop depth across one grid (needs the single grid). Also a new per-district danger tier or DepthBias column, which is extra data on top of the Zones override.

decisions.decision: Nav row: keep dynamic runtime navmesh with the default TileSizeUU 1000 and no invokers. setup_stage.py sizes ONE NavMeshBoundsVolume to the union of district rectangles plus margin, so the yard is navmeshed and the truck-to-gate paths can be checked. On the host, StartNight defers itself with a retry timer while the navigation build is in progress, and logs the wait. This needs no UI.
decisions.rationale: The map and its nav build happen in the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:270-271, 765-773). Nothing currently waits for nav before night start, and that gap is the real failure mode. With per-district ISM components, empty yard tiles scan no instances. Invokers either violate decision 4 or move the build into the night, and they are a global setting that would also change the other stages. The current code path stays: one box, just bigger.
decisions.rejected: Navigation invokers (violate decision 4 or move the build into the night). Per-slot volumes with no yard navmesh: kept as the fallback if the union build is too slow, because the union box is the existing path and makes the yard testable. A larger tile size up front: only after measurement.

decisions.decision: Rendering row: no HLOD and no district distance or visibility culling system in the first cut. Per-district actors give per-district components, so frustum and occlusion culling works per district. Log the lamp count and the flicker-lamp count next to the existing build log lines (CL9SiteMap.cpp:630-635). The fallback, only if yard-view GPU Lights/VolumetricFog is over budget, is MaxDrawDistance on lamps plus skipping TickFlicker beyond it (CL9SiteMap.cpp:286-303, 789-818). LampDensity stays the total-count lever.
decisions.rationale: performance.md:22/94 forbid optimisation before measurement. Collision must stay on every district on the server because far monsters walk against WorldStatic (decision 4). Ray tracing is already distance-culled at 300 m.
decisions.rejected: Per-district show/hide (it does not remove physics or nav cost, and toggling re-creates instance bodies). HLOD.

decisions.decision: Host monster cost under decision 4: AI, senses and movement always run. The monster MeshComponent sets VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered in C++ (only the player overrides it today, at CL9Character.cpp:147). No think-rate LOD and no distance sleep.
decisions.rationale: No CL9 C++ uses montages or notifies, and the only bone read is the cosmetic hit puff (CL9Monster.cpp:405). Movement is code-driven (AddActorWorldOffset), so skipping unseen poses does not change behaviour. OnlyTickMontages is chosen over OnlyTickPose in case a Blueprint uses montage notifies. Skeletal animation is the largest per-monster item (performance.md:118-119).
decisions.rejected: Think-rate LOD by distance. It can be read as distance throttling against decision 4, so if the measurement fails the fallback is lowering counts, not throttling.

decisions.decision: Population row and monster total: per district, roughly one Lethal interior. Base zone sums are about 9 (East/West), 11 (North/South) and 13 (far), about 53 in total. Through the existing MonsterCountCurve (0.6 on day 1, 1.0 on day 5, 1.5 on day 10, progression.md:29) that gives about 32 monsters on day 1, about 53 on day 5 and about 80 on day 10. Per district on day 10 that is about 13-20, against Titan's indoor 18 power at 1-3 power per enemy (lethal-map.md:204, lethal-monsters.md:595-629). Items keep the farm's per-module density (about 0.35 per module at base, farm.json:26-28), with far overrides weighted toward meat. Night spawning stays synchronous until it is measured; the fallback is time-sliced spawning.
decisions.rationale: This is a compromise between the nav-ai lens (about 45 / 80) and the play lens (35-40 / 90-100). It uses only existing data (Zones x day curve), with no new power system. It is about one third of a blind 5x of the farm (125 / 300), which user decision 4 rules out.
decisions.rejected: A Lethal-style power budget and spawn ramp (new code). 5x the farm density.

decisions.decision: Night row: NightLength 600, DarkBase 450, DarkMin 300 (the farm's 360/240 scaled by 600/480). One night, no multi-trip.
decisions.rationale: User decision 2. It keeps DarkMin <= DarkBase <= NightLength (stage.md:53), and the district size rule keeps every district within one night.
decisions.rejected: 30-50 min nights (from the original spec estimate).

decisions.decision: Walk-time row: do not add vehicles or shortcuts. Walk time is bounded by the per-district size rule plus jars. It is validated by a scripted walk truck -> gate -> deepest point -> nearest jar -> truck for each district.
decisions.rationale: The formula comes from only two data points (stage.md:58-59), so it must be checked by measurement.
decisions.rejected: Moving the truck, or several trips per night.

decisions.decision: Return jars row: SpecialCopies (the existing site column, inherited as 4 from farm) applies per district, because each layout reads Params.SpecialCopies. That gives about 4 delivery rooms per district, about 20 in all. The jar dedupe set in SpawnNight resets per district, since module indices are per layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:625-633).
